verdict.line: You lose if you eat free Shock Blast poke before level 3 and never close the gap; you win once you're in his face, because he has no hard CC to peel you off.

brief.thesis: Jayce's entire kit is built around keeping distance — Cannon Stance pokes, Hammer Stance only has a leap and a 240-range knockback to create separation, neither of which is a stun. Yorick heals through poke with Q (Last Rites) and can wall off his retreat with W (Dark Procession), so the matchup is a race to lane phase 3-5: whoever is ranged and uncommitted wins before that, whoever is melee and stuck in Mourning Mist wins after. The 53.8% win rate over 2115 games reflects that Yorick wins the lane once it goes to extended trades.

theirWindow.when: Jayce is in Cannon Stance, poking freely
theirWindow.what: Cannon Stance Q (Shock Blast) hits everything in its path for free damage with no commitment. Don't facecheck or walk into the lane center on cooldowns under 12s — eat it on minions and wait for him to swap stances or whiff before stepping up.

yourWindow.when: Jayce swaps to Hammer Stance and leaps in
yourWindow.what: Hammer Stance Q is a leap, not a poke — once he's used it to engage he's melee range and the leap is down for 16-8s depending on rank. Land E (Mourning Mist) for the armor shred and slow, then trade with empowered Q (Last Rites) autos; he only has a 240-range knockback to get back out.

start.why: The flat damage reduction on taking poke and the HP5 directly counters Jayce's auto-attack and Shock Blast chip before you hit level 3 and can trade back.

boots.why: Jayce's damage in this matchup is entirely basic-attack and Shock Blast physical poke — Steelcaps cut that down on every auto, ranged or melee.

core.why: Spellblade gives you a hard-hitting empowered auto to pair with Last Rites, and the stats (AD/AP/HP/move speed) close the range gap Jayce lives on.
Cooldown reduction stacks your Q and E faster, letting you chain Mourning Mist slows and graves more often in extended fights.
Armor shred plus the slow-on-hit stacks with Mourning Mist to make sure a Hammer Stance Jayce physically cannot walk away once he's tagged.

the game turns into a 1v9 splitpush and you need raw tower damage

you want extra burst and mobility to close the gap on a kiting jayce

runes.keystoneWhy: Every poke trade you take and every empowered Last Rites auto you land procs Grasp, turning Jayce's own poke pattern into sustain and max-health scaling for you — the higher-winrate page at 56.2% over the Conqueror alternative.

summoners.why: Teleport is the highest-pick option (69%) and lets you reset after shoving with your wall-and-poke trade pattern without giving up tempo; Flash+Ignite (53.2%, 20.1% pick) is the stronger choice if you want to force the level 3-5 all-in window into a kill.

playing.title: Don't trade before level 3
playing.detail: You have no gap-closer and Jayce's Cannon Stance Shock Blast is free damage. Farm behind minions until your full combo is up, matching OP.GG's own read on this matchup.

playing.title: All-in the moment you hit 3
playing.detail: Open with E (Mourning Mist) for the armor shred, slow, and mark, then follow with Q (Last Rites) empowered autos. This is your first real kill window and the data backs an aggressive solo-kill edge here.

playing.title: Wall him in before he commits further
playing.detail: Drop W (Dark Procession) across his retreat path once he's melee range in Hammer Stance — his only disengage is a 240-range knockback, not a dash, so a well-placed wall traps him.

playing.title: Respect his level 6 transform
playing.detail: Jayce's R swaps stances and the first attack after transforming carries bonus armor/MR reduction or magic damage. Expect a burst spike right after he ults and don't greed a trade into it.

playing.title: Hold E for when he's already melee
playing.detail: Mourning Mist's slow is wasted on a Jayce who's still kiting at range. Save it for the moment he leaps in on Hammer Stance Q so he can't knock-back and reset.

playing.title: Push waves to force stance decisions
playing.detail: Jayce has to commit to either poke (Cannon) or burst (Hammer) — a fast-shoving Yorick wave denies him the farm he needs to freely swap stances every rotation.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning — stance tells, cooldown windows, and the all-in timing — is this brief's own tactical read, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful during early game as Jayce will apply pressure. After reaching level 3, use [E] to deal damage with [P]. Trap him inside [W] to try to kill him.
